advances: Auxiliary correction on one row with real boundary contacts and classical Brunn–Minkowski.

proof:
Fix a segment to a destination with $f(z_j)=0$. Every section along it has positive volume by convexity of $C$ and the endpoint fibers. In such a section any point of strictly negative margin gives a positive-volume residual, by mixing it with a small interior ball. The parameters with strictly negative points form a convex subset of $[0,1]$. They include a right neighborhood of zero, by combining a strict point at zero with any point at the destination. They exclude one. Let $t_j$ be their supremum. Compactness gives a limit of strict points at $t_j$ with margin at most zero. If $t_j<1$ and there were any strict point at $t_j$, mixing with the destination would extend positivity past $t_j$. If $t_j=1$, the destination has zero residual by hypothesis. Thus $t_j$ is the first exit, all closed residual points there have zero margin, and their section has zero volume because the continuous normal is nonzero.

The weights sum to one and $\sum_j\widehat\theta_j(b_j-p)=c^{-1}\sum_j\theta_j(z_j-p)=0$. The closed residual sections at the $b_j$ are nonempty and compact. Their weighted Minkowski sum lies in the closed residual at $p$, since $C\cap\lbrace\ell\le0\rbrace$ is convex. Closed and strict sections have equal volumes since their difference lies in a hyperplane with nonzero continuous normal. Brunn–Minkowski, including for nonempty zero-volume summands by continuity, gives $f(p)\ge\sum_j\widehat\theta_jf(b_j)$. For the zero-residual destinations $f(b_j)=0$. For the others $b_j=z_j$ and $t_j=1$. Multiply by $c$ and use $\sum_j\theta_j=1$ to obtain the formula.
statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be compact convex, $d\ge1$, and write $C_z$ for its fiber over $z$. Let $H=\lbrace(z,x):\ell(z,x)\ge0\rbrace$ be a closed affine halfspace whose continuous normal is nonzero, and set $f(z)=|C_z\cap\lbrace\ell(z,x)<0\rbrace|^{1/d}$. Suppose $p=\sum_j\theta_jz_j$ with finitely many $\theta_j>0$, $\sum_j\theta_j=1$, positive $d$-volume fibers at $p,z_j$, and $f(p)>0$. If $f(z_j)>0$, set $t_j=1$ and $b_j=z_j$. Otherwise let $b_j=p+t_j(z_j-p)$ be the first exit from the positive residual projection on the segment to $z_j$. For each index with $f(z_j)=0$, one has $0<t_j\le1$ and $C_{b_j}\cap\lbrace\ell(b_j,x)\le0\rbrace$ is nonempty with volume zero. With $c=\sum_j\theta_j/t_j$, the weights $\widehat\theta_j=\theta_j/(ct_j)$ form a probability row of mean $p$ on the $b_j$. Moreover
$$
\sum_{j:f(z_j)>0}\theta_jf(z_j)
\le c f(p)
= f(p)+ f(p)\sum_{j:f(z_j)=0}\theta_j(1/t_j-1).
$$
title: First-exit correction for a residual-root barycentric row
